_comment: GRASS-FIELD. The camera-relative ground cover, and the flag that decides whether it or the baked scatter owns the ground plane. See scripts/world/grass_field.gd and shaders/grass_field.gdshader for the mechanism, and ralph/reports/WORLD_GRASS_2026-08-25.md for the measurement that forced it: a continuous carpet is ~40x outside the chapter's placement ceiling however it is spent, so no density number in vegetation.json reaches the reference. ALL OF THIS IS TUNABLE.
_comment_enabled: OFF BY DEFAULT, deliberately, and this is the whole safety story for the change. The one thing no container in this project can measure is the only hardware that matters -- PERF-ROG-GPU records that the Compatibility renderer counts MultiMesh batches rather than instances and that this box rasterises in software. So the owner has to be able to switch between the two ground systems on the Ally itself, and a bad handheld result has to be one boolean away from gone rather than a revert. Turn on to evaluate; do not turn on by default until a handheld pass says it is affordable.
_comment_enabled_ownerplaytest_20260901: The Ally said no. Owner playtest 2026-09-01, item 2 (named a game breaker): 'Severe lag -- frame rate collapsed to ~10 FPS.' This flag had been true since 181b7bf4 (2026-08-27, 'turn it on for handheld evaluation') and every number layered on top of it since (tuft_count to its own test-pinned ceiling of 300000, the 90000-stone tier, three cover tiers) shipped NOT MEASURED on real hardware, exactly as every comment in this file already warned. Measured here with tools/perf_render_stats.gd (real RenderingServer counters -- structural, not this box's meaningless software-rasteriser frame time) at band1_open, same bake, only this flag changed: enabled=true submits 31,757,567 primitives/frame; enabled=false submits 9,250,290. The field alone is 22,507,277 of them -- 71% of everything the frame draws -- entirely from grass_field.gd's own MultiMeshes, which carry no per-instance distance culling: every tuft/stone/bush/flower/litter item in the ring is submitted every frame regardless of what the camera is actually looking at. Draw calls barely move (7320 -> 7366, confirming PERF-ROG-GPU's finding that Compatibility counts MultiMesh batches, not instances) -- the cost is entirely vertex/fragment throughput, which is exactly the GPU-bound failure mode a software-rasterised container was always going to be blind to and a handheld iGPU was always going to feel. A cut that stays proportionate to what shipped (halving a few counts) would still leave multiple millions of unmeasured, uncullable primitives riding on the same architecture that just produced a ~10fps game-breaker with no way to verify a smaller number is safe without another real-device round trip the owner already spent on this one. So this reverts to the documented default rather than guessing at a smaller 'on' number: OFF, which is the exact contingency this flag and its suppression list were built for, and which is provably a 3.4x primitive cut back to the corridor's previously-shipped, never-flagged-as-laggy baseline. Re-enabling is still the owner's call and still one boolean -- but a real fix for the 71%-of-the-frame problem (actual per-instance/tile distance culling, not just smaller counts at the same uncullable architecture) is unbuilt, and belongs in front of the flag next time, not behind it.
_comment_enabled_ownerplaytest_20260902: OWNER-0902-GRASS-RENDER. Owner playtest 2026-09-02 item 1 asked whether 'no grass' is the intended effect of the above (it is -- this flag is still false) or whether a cheaper middle path exists instead of the all-or-nothing choice. It does, partially: the counts below (tuft_count, blades_per_tuft, blade_segments, stones.count, and the three cover_tiers' counts) were cut hard -- not the 'halving a few counts' the 2026-09-01 note already rejected as unprovable, but roughly a 4-5x cut on every one of them at once -- and re-measured the same way, tools/perf_render_stats.gd at band1_open: 13,692,485 primitives with the flag on, against 9,204,537 with it off and the 31,757,567 that produced the game-breaker. That is a ~5x cut in the field's own contribution (22.5M -> ~4.5M) and leaves the whole scene at 43% of the config that broke the Ally, for 49% more than shipping with the field off. A player-eye-level screenshot at the same site (band1_open) still shows a real, legible grass carpet -- tufts, clover-like ground cover and pale flowers at visible density, not a bald field -- so this is not merely a cheaper number, it still looks like grass at a glance. What this does NOT do: build the actual per-instance/tile distance culling the 09-01 note says is the real fix, and it does NOT clear a real-device A/B, which PERF-ROG-GPU still records as the only measurement this container cannot produce, or a blind visual-judge pass against the project's own reference art, which every other density change in this file has gone through. So the flag stays FALSE here -- turning it on is still exactly the owner's call the flag exists to reserve -- but the numbers it now guards are the measured-cheaper set rather than the ones that broke the Ally, so the next handheld A/B starts 5x lighter than the last one instead of repeating it. Full numbers and the screenshot are in ralph/reports/OWNER-0902-GRASS-RENDER.md. If the owner wants the old, denser 'always intended to look like' numbers back for a from-scratch handheld pass instead, they are tuft_count 300000 / blades_per_tuft 6 / blade_segments 4 / stones.count 90000 / cover_tiers bushes.count 14800 / flowers.count 14800 / litter.count 49000 -- recorded here because they are no longer what ships.
_comment_enabled_ownerplaytest_20260902b: OWNER-0902-GRASS-ON. Direct owner decision, 2026-09-02, verbatim: 'grass needs to be on.' Not a proposal weighed against the 'still the owner's call' language the note above left in place -- that call has now been made, overriding it. This flips the flag on the measured-cheaper config the note above prepared for exactly this: no numbers below changed. The primitive count is re-confirmed identical at flip time (see ralph/reports/OWNER-0902-GRASS-ON.md) and a real-device Ally A/B is still the one measurement no container in this project can produce -- PERF-ROG-GPU still applies, and if a future handheld pass says this is too expensive, the smaller number to fall back to is a config edit, not a revert of this flag.
_comment_suppress:
Which vegetation.json layers vegetation.gd skips while the field is on, so the two systems never both dress the same ground. `grass`/`drygrass`/`flowers` are the whole non-colliding carpet the field's own tuft ring actually replaces -- everything NOT in this list stays scatter and must: you collide with trees, rocks and bushes, you harvest them, and they are the landmarks the eye navigates by.

T1-GROUND, 2026-08-30: `groundmat` was landed here on consolidation (see git history for the note that used to be here) on the reasoning that the field 'also replaces' it, but the field carries no equivalent -- `cover_tiers` below is bushes/flowers/litter, nothing clover- or broadleaf-shaped. So with the field on, `vegetation.json`'s clover/broadleaf mid-layer (the ground->mat->tuft->canopy ladder its own `_comment` describes) was being thrown away with nothing standing in for it, which is most of why a blind visual pass ranked 'one grass species everywhere, every band the same vertical blade sprite' its top ground defect. Un-suppressing costs no re-bake (vegetation.gd reads this list at LOAD time, off the already-baked placements -- scatter_bake.gd's fingerprint does not cover this file) and no new asset: the 145,577 already-placed Clover_1/Clover_2/Plant_1_Big instances just render again, at the tint/scale/LOD `groundmat` already specifies, as the second silhouette family under the tuft carpet.
_comment_suppress_drygrass:
T1-GROUND-3, 2026-08-30: `drygrass` leaves this list, and it is the SECOND GRASS SPECIES the 2026-08-29 blind pass ranked as the ground's top defect -- 'every band uses the same vertical blade sprite at the same density; bands differ only by tree props and flower confetti'. The field's tuft ring is ONE generated blade shape (grass_field.gd::_tuft_mesh, six tapered strips at different yaws) and no amount of tint or density on it can be a second plant, so the second species has to come from a mesh, and CLAUDE.md forbids new Meadows art -- which leaves the installed nature pack, which already has one: `drygrass` carries Grass_Wispy_Short/Tall (a splayed fan) and Grass_Wheat (upright stalks with seed heads) under a straw retint. It was suppressed on the same reasoning `groundmat` was, and it is wrong for the same reason: `cover_tiers` below is bushes/flowers/litter, and none of those is a grass. What the field genuinely replaces is the layer whose silhouette IS its own -- `grass` (Grass_Common/Grass_Wide, upright blades), which stays suppressed. `flowers` stays too: the field's own flower tier replaces it shape for shape.

Un-suppressing alone costs no re-bake (vegetation.gd reads this list at LOAD time). The retune that goes with it -- taller than the field carpet so the tussocks break its top line rather than hiding under it, tighter clumps at a held instance count, and a per-band gradient so the dry species thickens toward the stronghold -- is in vegetation.json and DOES change the bake fingerprint; both landed in one commit with the bake.
_comment_ring: field_radius/fade_start/tuft_count are the three numbers that trade quality for cost, and none of them needs a re-bake. A blind pass measured the ground cover ending at about 40m as `a hard line across the hill, not a fade`, with painted khaki terrain and small dark blobs beyond it. So the ring reaches 72m and fades over the last 30 rather than the last 14. tuft_count rises with it but not in proportion: 300,000 over the larger disc is about 18 tufts/m2 against the old 21, which is the deliberate trade -- an edge you cannot see costs less than three more tufts per square metre in the near field. UNMEASURED ON THE DEVICE: this is a 43% vertex increase on the most expensive tier, and PERF-ROG-GPU records that no container in this project can measure GPU cost. It is the first number to cut if the Ally says no.
_comment_edge: How the carpet ENDS, which is a separate defect from where it ends. The owner's words on the last capture were that the transition from real grass to paint is still very noticeable, after field_radius had already been pushed 56 -> 72 to move it. It moved and did not go, because thinning the blades leaves the survivors at FULL HEIGHT: the carpet stops rather than runs out. `edge_shorten_floor` is the height multiplier at the outermost blade and `edge_shorten_bias` the curve -- below 1.0 it holds full height through most of the 30m fade and takes it off over the last part, so the carpet sinks into the terrain instead of being docked a third of its height where the player is actually looking. Free: one pow over a varying the shader already computes.
_comment_snap: Metres the ring snaps to as it follows the camera, and -- since GRASS-REROLL -- the size of the world LATTICE CELL every tier is laid out on. Deliberately one number for both: the node may only ever sit on whole cells, and two numbers that did not divide each other would silently reintroduce the defect below while looking perfect in a still frame. NOT A LOOK PARAMETER, and none of the five below are either. The defect: the owner played the build on 2026-08-28 and reported `the grass rerenders like every step`. It did. Every per-item property in the three field shaders is hashed on the item's WORLD position, and the ring moves, so a move re-rolled which tufts survive, how tall they are and which way they lean. Snapping never removed that -- it made it periodic, one whole-field re-roll every 2 metres, which at combat.json's 5 m/s walk is one every 0.4 seconds. The fix is in scripts/world/grass_field.gd's STABLE RING note: items stand on a world lattice, the node moves in whole cells, and where an item stands is hashed from the cell rather than from the ring, so stepping forward hands a cell to a different instance which draws exactly what the last one did. Larger cells are cheaper to plan and coarser at every layer's edge; smaller ones quantise the per-cell item counts badly on the sparse tiers.
_comment_lattice: How the nested lattices that carry `centre_bias`'s density gradient are scheduled. A single uniform lattice cannot have a gradient, and the gradient is most of why the near field reads as thick -- 0.62 puts ~78 tufts/m2 at the eye against ~15 at the rim -- so the ring is a base lattice over the whole disc plus a stack of smaller discs each adding the difference. `lattice_layer_ratio` is how much smaller each disc is than the last (1.5 fits the disc law to within a few per cent everywhere the player can see; larger is fewer layers and a coarser fit), `lattice_band` is the fraction of a disc's radius at which it is still fully present so the rest is its growth band, and `lattice_min_radius` is where the stack stops -- below about two metres the ring is under the camera and the tufts there are not in any frame. `lattice_jitter` is how much of its own cell an item may wander: 1.0 fills the cell, which is what makes a lattice read as scatter rather than as rows, and 0 would put every item dead centre and make the grid plainly visible. `lod_dither` is the width in rank of a layer's growth band -- small means each item grows in fast but few are growing at once, large the reverse. It is the only knob here that trades one kind of visible change for another.
_comment_blade: One tuft is `blades_per_tuft` tapered strips at different yaws, generated in code by grass_field.gd::_tuft_mesh -- no asset enters the repository, which keeps CLAUDE.md's no-new-assets rule for the Meadows untouched. `blade_segments` is how many quads make a blade; more bends more smoothly and costs triangles linearly. Heights are in metres against the 1.80m trainer: WORLD-GRASS landed the scattered tufts at a 0.71m mean and a blind critic still called them short, so this starts a little above that and grows with distance so a far blade stays a few pixels tall instead of shimmering.
_comment_coverage: What stops this being a lawn. `density_gain` is the flat keep-chance; `clump_scale` is the frequency of the drift noise that modulates it (smaller is broader drifts) and `clump_contrast` how hard that noise bites -- 0 is uniform coverage, 1 is drifts with genuinely bare ground between them. This is where GROUND-LAYERS' measured composition target lives now: roughly 70% open grass, 15% path/worn, 10% low accents, 5% special. That target was expressed as placement counts before and cannot be any more, so it is expressed as noise here. TUNABLE, and the first thing to re-judge against a blind pass.
_comment_colour: Derived from measurement, not by eye. Sampled off-route on WORLD-GRASS's own frames, the meadow's ground reads #798732 (hue 68.3, value 0.529) against the owner reference's foreground grass at #7c8737 (hue 68.4, value 0.529) -- the palette was already right, so these sit around it rather than replacing it. `ground_blend` is the fix for the defect three blind rounds named: it mixes the terrain's OWN colour map into the base of every blade, so growth appears to come out of the ground instead of standing on a picture of it. `translucency` fakes the light through a blade; the Compatibility renderer has no subsurface scattering, so it lifts the tip rather than pretending to transmit.
_comment_wind: Free here, and the owner's reference frames are of moving grass. Strength is in metres of tip travel.
_comment_gust: GUST-WAVE. A travelling front on top of the ambient breeze, rather than the whole field leaning together -- which reads as a wobble where a gust crossing the meadow reads as weather. `gust_speed` is metres per second of front travel and `gust_length` its wavelength in metres, so 7.0 and 26.0 is a front crossing the visible field about every four seconds. Free: it is one sine over a dot product the shader already has. The owner reference frames are of moving grass and this is the half of that motion a per-item noise cannot give.
_comment_stones: STONE-FIELD. Loose grit, gravel and field stone, on the SAME camera-relative ring as the grass and storing nothing either. It exists because a blind pass, asked directly whether stones, path edges and tree bases read as bedded into the ground or sitting on top of it, answered: 'No -- everything sits on top. This is the single most consistent failure in the set.' It measured the band-4 cobbles as flat-topped slabs with their entire edge exposed, none partially buried, none casting a contact shadow; and it found the path shares one texture with the meadow, 'so the boundary is a density edge rather than a material edge, and it looks cut', with a surface that at 1-3m is 'a repeating mottled blob pattern with no grain, gravel, dirt clod, rut or footprint'. This is the path's own surface and the answer to both. `ground` names where stone is ALLOWED and is built from the same terrain texture list the grass field builds its FORBIDDEN mask from, so the two are inverses by construction and tile the ground between them. `stray_chance` is what stops the gravel ending on the same hard line the grass mask was criticised for -- a few field stones out on ordinary meadow. `sink` is the whole bedded argument in one number: the fraction of its own height a stone is buried, so its lower edge is under the surface instead of standing proud of it all the way round. `contact_darken` is the occlusion a stone this small will never get from the shadow map. TUNABLE, and the whole tier is one `enabled` away from gone.
_comment_cover_tiers: The generic plant tiers on the same ring: small bushes, flower drifts, forest litter. Each is one MultiMesh child running shaders/cover_tier.gdshader, differing only by mesh and numbers -- see that shader's header for the rule about WHAT may be generated this way. Short version: a tier qualifies only if it does not collide, carries no persistent state, is small enough that appearing at the ring's edge is invisible, and exists in numbers too large to store. Trees and boulders fail three of those -- they are landmarks, they stop the camera's SpringArm, and they must be where you left them. HARVESTABLE bushes fail the state test: vegetation.json's `bushes` layer carries harvest_item fiber, and harvesting needs an identity that survives, which a thing that does not exist until the camera nears it cannot have. So these bushes are DECORATIVE understorey and the harvestable ones stay scattered. tests/test_grass_field.gd enforces that half of the rule against vegetation.json directly. Each tier draws from its own RNG stream so adding or removing one cannot reshuffle where any other tier's items land.
_clearing: Where the bush tier gathers, the grass thins and shortens. The grass and the cover tiers are separate MultiMeshes that know nothing about each other, so without this they occupy the same ground and blades stand straight through leaves -- the owner's words were that the grass overlaps the bushes. grass_field.gd reads the shape of the field off whichever tier sets `clears_grass`, so the thinning cannot drift away from the bushes it is thinning for. `clearing_floor` is high on purpose: the drift runs about 0.12-1.0 and the bushes take only a fraction of even its strongest part, so clearing everywhere above average would thin a third of the meadow for the sake of a tenth of it.

cover_tiers._why: Small bushes. A blind pass found the world jumps from 50cm grass straight to 6m canopy with nothing between -- 'a forest you can see straight through at knee height' -- and counted two mid-height plants across twelve frames. This is that missing band. Sparse and heavily drifted on purpose: understorey gathers, it does not carpet, and the meadow's negative space is what GROUND-LAYERS measured as worth keeping.
cover_tiers.name: bushes
cover_tiers._comment_count_ring: Scaled with the ring: field_radius 56 -> 72 is 1.65x the disc, so a count held constant would have thinned every generated tier by a third at the same moment the ring stopped being visible.
cover_tiers._comment_contact: Was 0.14, which was itself a correction after a round where the bushes read as dark blobs. Raised because a blind pass measured the opposite failure at the boundary -- 'no contact darkening where they meet the ground' -- and because the correction is different in kind now: leaf_root_darken below carries the internal shading that 0.14 was trying not to overdo, so the bush no longer needs its whole base lifted to avoid reading as a blob.
cover_tiers._comment_leaf_cut: The fix four rounds of tuning could not reach. Each leaf is a quad and a rectangle does not read as a leaf however it is lit -- so cover_tier.gdshader carves a ragged leaf outline out of every quad in the fragment stage. 1.0 is the full cut. Costs no asset, which is why it is the right instrument: CLAUDE.md forbids new Meadows art and the last blind round filed this as an art gap.
cover_tiers._comment_leaf_shade: The SECOND half of the same defect, and a different one from the outline. With the quads cut to leaf shapes a blind pass stopped calling the bushes a heap of flat quads and started calling them flat clipart with zero shading gradient -- because tint_base/tint_tip run up the whole BUSH, so every leaf in one ring shares an albedo and the ring reads as a band of one flat fill. leaf_root_darken shades each leaf dark at its stem and lit at its tip; leaf_tint_jitter stops any two being quite the same. Both read the UV2 the outline mask already fetches.
cover_tiers._comment_wood: The branches the owner asked for. tint_wood is what the trunk and the six arcing sticks take instead of the leaf gradient -- a dry olive-brown rather than a tree bark, because at 0.85m tall these are shrub twigs seen against grass, and a true bark brown reads as a stick lying in the field.
cover_tiers._comment_scatter_finding_t1_world: T1-WORLD, five rounds, REVERTED to the values above this comment's arrival and kept here only as the record of why. The blind pass's 'ground scatter reads procedural -- a near-constant ~1m interval, no clustering, no bare patch' is NOT about this system, and five rounds of tuning these numbers changed nothing measurable because they were aimed at the wrong place. `suppress_scatter_layers` above is the whole explanation: this field takes over `grass` and `flowers` and NOTHING ELSE, so the broadleaf rosettes the judge described -- vegetation.json's `bushes` layer (Bush_Common, Bush_Common_Flowers, Fern_1) and `groundmat` (Clover_1/2, Plant_1_Big) -- are still baked scatter placed by scatter_rules.gd, and no value in this file reaches them. The measurements, so nobody repeats the five rounds: flower-pixel coefficient of variation over a 14x6 grid on the elevated frames went 3.88 -> 3.65 (village), 1.03 -> 1.06 (band1), 1.96 -> 1.77 (band4) across the whole sequence -- within noise, in both directions, at every setting tried including a peaky drift_gate at the density_gain ceiling. What IS true and worth keeping from those rounds is the mechanism analysis, which applies to both systems: a keep-roll that is an independent Bernoulli trial per site over a linearly-remapped noise mask is a near-Poisson point process, and Poisson has a characteristic spacing and no clustering by construction. cover_tier.gdshader's new `drift_gate` is that fix for THIS system, left at its 1.0 default (a no-op) because there is no evidence it is needed here. The same fix aimed at the baked layers needs a re-bake, which is coordinator-owned (GATE_D_LANE_CONTRACT sec4).

cover_tiers._why: Flower drifts. The defect this answers was measured rather than judged: a blind pass counted flowers appearing EXACTLY TWICE in twelve frames, both the same violet bush asset, each 'a single isolated ball of saturated violet with a hard base', against moong-02 running a pink drift across ~40% of frame width and the keyart putting purple, gold and white wildflowers in every panel. The numbers here are shaped by that: a LOW drift_scale (0.03) means broad patches rather than a sprinkle, and a high drift_contrast means genuinely empty ground between them. Prompt 72 asked for the same thing in its own words -- 'the reference pink drifts are tight and irregular'. Colour is the one place this tier deliberately leaves the meadow palette: palette.json reserves flower_gold #d9b340 as an accent and the keyart carries lilac, so the bloom is lilac over an olive stalk. It is NOT oxblood and must never drift toward it -- that red is reserved for Team Tether and three blind passes have confirmed the reservation is still clean.
cover_tiers.name: flowers

cover_tiers._why: Forest litter. Band 2 is called forest floor and a blind pass found it carrying meadow grass and sand under the trees -- 'no leaf litter, no needles, no moss, no fungi, no fallen branches' -- and separately that 'a player walking these four bands would not know the region had changed'. This is the band-differentiating dressing, and it is restricted to the forest_floor ground type so it appears where the terrain already says there are trees rather than being scattered everywhere and hoping. slope_lie 1.0 lays it ON the ground following the gradient, which is what makes litter read as litter and not as flat cards standing on a slope; sway 0 because leaves on the ground do not move in a breeze.
cover_tiers.name: litter
cover_tiers._comment_leaf_cut: Same mask as the bushes, and for the same reason: the mesh comment calls these scraps irregular and as opaque squares they were not. Slightly gentler and coarser-toothed than the bush leaf so a fallen leaf reads as broader than a growing one.

_comment_far_cover: FAR COVER, and the answer to the meadow ENDING at 72m. `field_radius` puts the last blade there and beyond it the ground is painted terrain with the surviving scatter on it, which from the `03-rise-overlook` viewpoint reads as a line across the hill -- the world stops where the ring does. `_comment_ring` above records the two answers already spent on that same line: the ring pushed 40 -> 56 -> 72m, the last step a 43% vertex increase on the most expensive tier in the game and UNMEASURED ON THE DEVICE. The owner has since played it on the Ally and said the grass already feels expensive, so the ring does not move a third time and nothing beyond it is made of blades. This is the cheap instrument instead: one terrain-following sheet, blended over the ground, carrying the meadow's cover READ -- hue, value, the same drifts, a mottle -- and none of its geometry. At the ranges it is visible that is all real grass would have been contributing anyway. ONE SHEET, ONE DRAW: `grass_field.gd` prints its triangle count at boot, and it is a fraction of a per cent of the grass tier's. What it costs that this box cannot measure is FILL -- one blended layer over ground the frame was already drawing -- and `PERF-ROG-GPU` records that GPU cost is exactly what no container here can measure. `enabled` false is the whole revert.
_comment_far_edges: The two edges, and the rule that governs them: do not trade one hard line for two. `fade_in_start`/`fade_in_end` bring the sheet up INSIDE the grass ring's own 42-72m fade, so the two systems hand over inside each other instead of meeting -- at 52m the grass is still at about four fifths of its coverage, which is what the sheet arrives behind. `fade_out_start`/`far_radius` take it away again over a band four times as wide as the one it arrived over, and that asymmetry is the whole argument: the near hand-over has real grass to hide behind, the far one has only its own slowness, the aerial perspective in art.json, and the fact that ground at 320m+ from an overlook eye is a few pixels tall. `far_radius` is also the sheet's cost: triangles go as its square. `far_cell` is the grid step, forced to a whole multiple of `snap` so the sheet can keep a fixed world grid while the ring hops (see FAR LATTICE in grass_field.gd); smaller follows the terrain more closely and costs quadratically, larger starts to cut through hillsides. `lift` is how far it is held above the sampled height, which is what stops the depth test eating it in patches between its samples -- sub-pixel at any range it is actually visible from.
_comment_far_look: What it draws, and the one measurement that shaped it. `strength` is peak opacity. The first version ran 0.55 over darker tints and the frames said two things: the mid band at 03-rise-overlook lost 11% of its EDGE ENERGY, and it went dark enough (lum -0.051) to become a local minimum between the near grass and the hazier distance -- a soft dark ring, which is the hard line again wearing a kinder edge. Both have the same cause: a blend at `strength` dilutes whatever texture the ground already had by exactly that fraction, so a wash carrying no texture of its own leaves the far meadow SMOOTHER and DARKER than it found it, which is the original defect with a green cast. So the tints here are lighter than the grass tier's (a hillside of grass is mostly the shaded side of a blade and the ground between, but a hillside seen through 200m of air is not as dark as a blade), and `mottle_value` gives the mottle authority over BRIGHTNESS rather than hue alone, which is what pays the diluted contrast back. `mottle_scale` sets the coarse feature size, `mottle_detail` adds a second octave at about three times the frequency, and `mottle_detail_range` is where that octave stops -- a one-metre feature at 400m is smaller than a pixel and turns into crawling speckle under minification rather than reading as ground. The noise is evaluated PER FRAGMENT, not per vertex: the sheet's vertices are 6m apart and the mottle's finest feature is about a metre, so a per-vertex mottle undersamples itself six times over and contributes nothing, which is exactly what the first version did. The DRIFTS are not configured here on purpose -- grass_field.gd pushes `clump_scale` and `clump_contrast` in verbatim, so the far ground's open patches are the same world-space patches the near field's are rather than a second pattern shaped to look similar. Two similar patterns meeting is the line again. `ground_blend` multiplies the terrain's own colour map in, exactly as the grass tier does and for the same reason its comment gives.

far_cover._comment_dilate_lift: T1-GROUND-3. THE DASHED SEAM LINES, root-caused to this sheet and fixed here. Full mechanism, the two hypotheses it displaces and the numbers behind both are in far_cover.gdshader's own uniform comment and in tools/_probe_ground_seams.gd, which measures it headlessly in about a minute. Short version: `lift` is measured from a vertex's own height sample, the sheet between vertices is a chord, and the ground bulges over that chord -- at the five capture viewpoints 3.3% of this sheet's cells had terrain standing through them, 10.6% at band 1, and because the sheet's grid is fixed and world-axis-aligned those holes line up into the rows of dashes two blind passes reported. This raises each vertex above its own half-cell neighbourhood max instead, which leaves flat ground sitting at `lift` exactly as before and lifts only where the ground is lumpy: measured 3.28% -> 1.19% for eight per-VERTEX texture fetches, no triangles. The value is the CAP on what the dilation may add, so a cliff cannot carry a whole cell up with it; 0.0 restores the previous behaviour exactly. TUNABLE.

_comment_built: BUILT GROUND, and the answer to the owner's 2026-08-28 report that `grass grows through indoor buildings now`. `forbidden_ground` below is a terrain TEXTURE mask, and a texture name cannot know that a farmhouse is standing on the grass it names -- so the field grew up through Grandpa's floor and his rug the day it was switched on. The building list is NOT duplicated here: scripts/world/grass_field.gd reads vegetation.json's own `footprints`, the same list scatter_rules.gd has gated every baked placement on since the identical defect was found in the scatter (that file's entries say so in their own words -- `grass was standing on the floor and the rug`). Two lists of building positions would be one edit away from disagreeing and the way you would find out is grass on a rug. What IS tunable here is the runtime half: `built_clear_ids` names which player-built pieces count as ground that has been covered over. A floor panel is exactly that and grass through it is the reported defect; a fence rail or a workbench is a thing STANDING in the meadow, and clearing a disc of grass around one would read as a scorch mark -- so they are deliberately absent. `built_piece_radius` is build_grid.gd's 2.0m cell half-diagonal: the circle that covers a panel completely. The inscribed 1.0m circle does not -- four of them around a shared corner leave that corner bare of cover, and a floor grid would sprout a tuft at every corner in a regular pattern, which is a worse artefact than the one being fixed.
_comment_forbidden: Ground the field refuses, by terrain texture NAME rather than by id. terrain_playground.json's `textures` array order is what assigns the ids (0 grass, 1 soil, 2 rock, 3 path, 4 damp, 5 forest_floor), so naming them means a lane that reorders that list does not silently move the mask onto the wrong surface. `path` is what keeps the routes readable -- the same control map the terrain paints its dirt from, so the verge lines up with the road for free instead of being a second exclusion rule that has to be kept in sync.
